षट्—कर्मन् n. the six duties of Brāhmans (viz. अध्ययन, ‘studying or repeating the Veda’, अध्यापन, ‘teaching the V˚’, यजन ‘offering sacrifices’, याजन, ‘conducting them for others’, दान, ‘giving’, and प्रतिग्रह, ‘accepting gifts’), ŚāṅkhGṛ.; Mn. &c. (the six daily duties accord. to the later law-books, are, स्नान, ‘religious bathing’, संध्याजप, ‘repetition of prayers at the three Saṃdhyās’, ब्रह्म-यज्ञ, ‘worship of the Supreme Being by repeating the first words of sacred books’, तर्पण, ‘daily oblations of water to the gods, sages, and Pitṛs’, होम, ‘oblations of fuel, rice &c. to fire’, देव-पूजा, ‘worship of the secondary gods either in the domestic sanctuary or in temples’), Parāś.; RTL. 394

six acts any one of which is allowable to a Brāhman householder as a means of subsistence (viz. ऋत, ‘gleaning’, अमृत, ‘unsolicited alms’, मृत, ‘solicited alms’, कर्षण, ‘agriculture’, सत्यानृत, ‘commerce or trade’, श्व-वृत्ति, ‘servitude’, the last being condemned), Mn. iv, 4, 5, 6, 9
six acts belonging to the practice of Yoga (viz. धौती, वस्ती, नेती, त्राटक, नौलिक, कपाल-भाती, these consist of suppressions of the breath and self-mortifications of various kinds), Cat.

six acts for inflicting various kinds of injury on enemies (viz. शान्ति, वश्य, स्तम्भन, विद्वेष, उच्चाटन, मारण, qq.vv.; these acts consist in repeating certain magical spells and texts taught in the Tantras), ib.

साट्टाल m. or n. (?) a palace (v.l. for साद्दाल), Bhadrab.
स-टंकार mfn. (fr., 7. स + ट्˚) having notoriety or fame, famous, MW.
सटालु = शलाटु, an unripe fruit, PārGṛ.
सट्टक—टीका f. N. of wk.
सट्टय—व्याख्या f. N. of wk.
सट्वा f. and kind of bird, L.
a musical instrument, L.
साटोप mfn. puffed up, self-conceited, proud, arrogant, Vās.
rumbling (as clouds), Pañcat.
साटोपम् (अम्), ind. haughtily, Mṛcch.; Ratnāv.
with a rumbling sound, Śiś.
angrily, furiously, MW.
साट्टहास mfn. with loud laughter (अम् ind.), MārkP.
साट्टहासम् ind.
